researched.name: Smarty
researched.description: USPS and international address verification, autocomplete, geocoding and property-data APIs for developers, with a government line selling cleaner address data to public agencies
researched.notes: Horizontal developer-API company: USPS/international address verification, autocomplete, geocoding and property data sold to any business that has an address field, with government as one vertical line among many. Product company, but the government cut is a segment of a general-purpose data API — not a system built for agencies. Rule 6 / horizontal shape, queue for a person rather than force it onto a public SLED board.

researched.name: Snowflake
researched.description: Cloud data platform for storing, processing, analysing and sharing data and building AI applications on it, sold to enterprises and, through a public sector practice, to government agencies.
researched.notes: Named in the brief as the archetype: a general-purpose cloud data platform sold to every industry, with a public-sector go-to-market on top. Not a govtech product company, not a supplier either.

researched.name: Socure
researched.description: AI identity verification and fraud-prevention platform, FedRAMP-authorized, sold to banks, businesses and government agencies.
researched.notes: Horizontal identity-verification and fraud platform whose primary market is banks, fintechs and online businesses; FedRAMP authorization and agency deals make government one buyer among everyone else. Same shape as the listed horizontals — not earned as govtech.

researched.name: Speridian
researched.description: IT consulting and low-code case management (CaseXellence) for public sector agencies, including state health and human services programmes, alongside banking, insurance and retail practices.
researched.notes: Named product: CaseXellence. Rule 2 exception survives, but the category does not. Confirmed: Speridian is a global consulting and technology services firm (advisory, implementation, managed services) spanning banking, insurance, retail, manufacturing, healthcare, real estate and government — a consultancy by identity. It clears the rule 2 exception because it licenses genuinely named products, and CaseXellence is verifiably licensed to public agencies rather than merely marketed: New Mexico Workers' Compensation Administration case management system, New Mexico Public Regulation Commission, New Mexico EPMO, plus a govern

researched.name: Splunk (Cisco)
researched.description: Data platform for security operations (SIEM, SOAR, UEBA) and IT observability, sold to enterprises and to state and local government and education.
researched.notes: Named in the brief as the archetype: horizontal SIEM/observability platform sold to enterprises worldwide, with SLED as one segment. Queue for a person.

researched.name: StackAI
researched.description: No-code platform for building, governing and deploying enterprise AI agents, sold to IT teams at organisations with regulated and complex operations
researched.notes: Horizontal no-code platform for building and governing enterprise AI agents, sold to IT teams at any regulated or complex organisation. Nothing agency-specific in the product; government would be one customer type among all others.

researched.name: STChealth
researched.description: Immunization information systems (STC|ONE) and vaccine data exchange for state and local public health immunization programs, pharmacies and providers.
researched.notes: Named product: STC|ONE. Survives. STC|ONE is the immunization information system that state and jurisdictional public health departments run their immunization registries on — South Dakota DOH launched its SDIIS on it, and STC has set national IIS standards with CDC since its Arizona Department of Public Health origin. Buyer is a public agency and the product is the programme system, so rule 5's test is passed on the merits, not by healthcare adjacency. Checked for scope_review and rejected it: STChealth also runs a pharmacy and pharma data-exchange channel (54,000+ provider and pharmacy partners, MyIR Mobile, IZ Gat

researched.name: Strategic Solutions Group
researched.description: Casetivity-based public health software - immunization information systems, electronic disease surveillance, early intervention, lead poisoning prevention and vital records - for state and local public health agencies.
researched.notes: Named product: Casetivity. Survives, and it is the cleanest of the four. SSG sells five fit-to-purpose applications on its own Casetivity platform — Electronic Disease Surveillance, Immunization Information System, Early Intervention Part C, Lead Poisoning Prevention, and Vital Records — as cloud subscriptions to state and local public health agencies. I tested the consultancy objection: SSG does list IT consulting, systems analysis, design/development and project management alongside the platform, so it is a hybrid. But Casetivity is its own named, licensed platform sold to public agencies, which clears rule 2's except

researched.name: TEKsystems
researched.description: IT services, systems integration and technology staffing, including healthcare IT delivery for payers and providers.
researched.notes: Rule 2 and the staffing clause: IT staffing, systems integration and delivery services — it sells people and hours, plus healthcare IT delivery for payers and providers. No software product of its own. Off the board, into suppliers.json.

researched.name: Telligen
researched.description: Utilization management, care management, quality measurement and PASRR services (Qualitrac) for state Medicaid agencies, federal health programmes and health plans.
researched.notes: A health management services business: utilization management, care management, quality measurement and PASRR reviews performed by its own clinical staff for federal programmes, state Medicaid agencies, employers/self-funded and Taft-Hartley plans, and health plans. Qualitrac is the platform its reviewers work in rather than the thing being bought, and a large share of the book is employer and health-plan work (Rule 4 territory). Torn between govtech and supplier, so per the asymmetry: supplier, reopenable if the state-Medicaid Qualitrac licensing turns out to be a standalone product sale.

researched.name: TransUnion
researched.description: Consumer credit, identity and risk data used for verification, fraud prevention and analytics, sold across industries that include healthcare and the public sector.
researched.notes: A consumer credit bureau selling identity, risk and analytics data across every industry, with public sector as one of many verticals. Classic horizontal — not a govtech product company.

researched.name: Truv
researched.description: Consumer-permissioned income, employment and asset verification APIs for mortgage and consumer lenders, tenant and background screeners, and public sector agencies verifying wage-earner and self-employment income
researched.notes: Horizontal fintech API for consumer-permissioned income, employment and asset verification; primary buyers are mortgage and consumer lenders and background/tenant screeners, with public-sector benefits eligibility as one added channel. Government is among everyone else, so it queues rather than lands on the board.

researched.name: Vault Technologies, Inc.
researched.description: Public health clinic and mass-vaccination software - IIS data transfer and interoperability, clinic management, school and community clinic planning, vaccination billing and consumer immunization record portals - for public health agencies.
researched.notes: Named product: PrepMod / PMEnterprise / OptimIIS / IISConnex. Survives, and I am supplying the product names the prior reviewer omitted — a govtech verdict should not rest on an unnamed product. VAULT sells PrepMod and PMEnterprise (mass vaccination), PMCommunity (community immunization), OptimIIS (IIS platform, HL7/FHIR), IISConnex (IIS-to-IIS data transfer), ReadiBilling, and the VAULT Interoperability Accelerator. Buyers are state health departments (PA/PhilaVax, WA IIS, MD, CO, ND, CA, RI, MT) and county health departments (Anoka, Dakota, Polk) — public agencies running their immunization programmes on the product, satisfying rule 5. I checked rule 4

researched.name: Verato
researched.description: Identity resolution and master data management software - person matching and provider data - for healthcare organizations and state and local government.
researched.notes: Identity resolution and MDM whose dominant market is healthcare organisations — health systems, payers, HIEs — which Rule 5 says is healthcare IT, not govtech, with state and local HHS agencies as an additional segment. A real product company selling to government among everyone else; torn between govtech and not, so it does not get the public card.

researched.name: Wiz
researched.description: Cloud and AI security platform connecting code, cloud and runtime into one risk graph, sold to enterprise security teams.
researched.notes: Horizontal cloud and AI security platform sold to enterprise security teams generally; a public-sector/FedRAMP line does not make the product govtech. Same shape as Splunk and Snowflake.

researched.name: Commence
researched.description: Fraud, waste and abuse detection, independent dispute resolution, peer review, patient advocacy and health-data transformation services for federal health agencies, state and local government and commercial payers.
researched.notes: Rule 2 (services business, not a product company). Site confirms a managed/professional-services firm — FWA reviews, independent dispute resolution, peer review, patient advocacy — delivered on an outcomes/managed-services basis, primarily to federal health buyers (CMS, VA, DHA) plus commercial payers. Technology is delivery infrastructure for its own service lines, not a named product licensed to SLED agencies.

researched.name: ConfigureTek
researched.description: ServiceNow implementation partner selling CMDB, service-mapping and ITSM accelerators plus managed services to enterprises, healthcare EMR shops and state, local and education buyers.
researched.notes: Rule 2 (consultancy/systems integrator). A ServiceNow implementation partner selling deployment work, 'accelerators' and managed services on top of someone else's platform — people and hours plus another vendor's product, which is also Rule 1 territory. No named software of its own licensed to agencies.

researched.name: Cotiviti
researched.description: Payment accuracy, risk adjustment and quality analytics for health plans, government healthcare programs and providers.
researched.notes: Rules 5 and 2. Payment-accuracy, risk-adjustment and quality analytics sold as an outsourced service, and the buyer is overwhelmingly health plans (commercial, MA, Medicaid MCOs) rather than a public agency. 'Government healthcare programs' here means payers administering those programs, not a system a state agency runs Medicaid on. Healthcare payer services, not govtech.

researched.name: CSG Government Solutions
researched.description: Program modernization consulting - project management, independent verification and validation, quality assurance and organizational change management - for state Medicaid, child welfare, child support, unemployment insurance and motor vehicle programs
researched.notes: Rule 2, textbook case. Program modernization consulting — project management, IV&V, QA, organizational change management. Sells people and hours to agencies; no licensed software product of its own.

researched.name: Databricks
researched.description: Unified data, analytics and AI platform — ETL, data warehousing, governance and ML/GenAI application development — sold to enterprises.
researched.notes: Named in the board's own rule as the shape of a horizontal vendor: a general data/AI/analytics platform sold to enterprises across every industry, with government as one segment. Not a call to force — queues for a person.

researched.name: Datadog
researched.description: Cloud observability, application monitoring and security SaaS for engineering and IT teams, offered to public agencies at FedRAMP High
researched.notes: Horizontal observability/monitoring SaaS sold to engineering teams in every industry; FedRAMP High authorization makes it available to public agencies but does not make it a govtech product. Same shape as Splunk. Queues for a person.

researched.name: Deloitte
researched.description: Audit, tax and consulting firm whose Government & Public Services practice sells program integrity services that detect, monitor and investigate fraud, waste and abuse in government health programs.
researched.notes: Rule 2 names Deloitte explicitly. Audit/tax/consulting firm; the Government & Public Services practice sells program-integrity and transformation services — people and hours — even where it runs state programs. No named licensed product claimed.

researched.name: Docket
researched.description: Consumer mobile and web app that pulls official immunization records out of state immunization registries for residents, sold to state and local public health agencies.
researched.notes: Named product: Docket (immunization records platform / resident-facing IIS portal and mobile app). Survives challenge. Rule 5 is the one to test here and it passes on the buyer test: the contracting customer is a public health authority, not a hospital or health system. docket.care lists ten agency partners (Alaska DOH, DC Health, Idaho DHW, Maine DHHS, Minnesota DOH, Missouri DHSS, New Jersey DOH, North Dakota DHHS, Utah DHHS, Wyoming DOH), each running a state-branded web app on Docket's platform layered over the state immunization registry. It is a product company, not a consultancy (Rule 2 n/a), not a reseller (Rule 1 n/a), and not employer-benefits (Rule 4 n/a - this is a system the ag

researched.name: Dun & Bradstreet, Inc.
researched.description: Business identity, risk and local-economy data and analytics sold to state and local government agencies.
researched.notes: Horizontal commercial data and analytics business — business identity, credit and risk data sold to every industry — with a /SLED landing page for its government vertical. Selling the same data assets to agencies among everyone else is the Databricks/Splunk shape, not a purpose-built govtech product. Queues for a person.

researched.name: Edifecs
researched.notes: Rule 6 on the record as given: no site and no description on file, so nothing in the intake justifies a card. What public material shows is a healthcare interoperability software vendor (EDI, encounter and enrollment management, FHIR) whose core customers are commercial health plans — reportedly all national plans and most of the top 25 commercial payers — with state Medicaid agencies as one vertical among them. That is the horizontal-sells-to-government-too shape, and it is now under Cotiviti. Not earned as govtech; a person should confirm whether the state Medicaid module business is the rea

researched.name: Elyon
researched.description: Public sector modernization consulting plus the CADET AI government-transformation platform, sold to state health and human services, Medicaid and child welfare agencies.
researched.notes: Rule 2, and the named-product exception does NOT rescue it. Site checked: Elyon Strategies is a management consulting firm (enterprise architecture, program management, OCM, executive coaching) for state HHS, Medicaid and child welfare clients. CADET is presented as a 'Government Transformation Intelligence' tool used inside their consulting delivery, not a standalone product licensed to agencies. Consulting engagement with an AI tool attached is still people and hours.

researched.name: Envision Technology Partners, Inc.
researched.description: WebIZ immunization information system for state and local immunization registries, now sold as part of InductiveHealth's public health platform.
researched.notes: Named product: WebIZ. Survives challenge. Rule 2 is the real risk - the company self-describes as a 'public health software development and consulting firm' - but this is precisely Rule 2's named-product exception, and the product is the business rather than a side-line to billable hours: WebIZ is a licensed SaaS immunization information system running the registries of 20+ CDC IIS awardee jurisdictions (state, local and tribal public health agencies), listed as a SaaS offer on Microsoft Marketplace, and Envision is the largest data contributor to CDC's IZ Gateway. Rule 5 passes on the buyer test - the customer is

researched.name: Epic
researched.description: Electronic health record and healthcare software used by academic medical centers, community hospitals, independent practices and payers.
researched.notes: Rule 5 is written for exactly this case: an EHR sold to academic medical centers, community hospitals, independent practices and payers is healthcare IT, not government technology. The buyer is a health system, not a public agency, even when that health system is publicly affiliated.

researched.name: Equifax
researched.description: Consumer credit bureau whose The Work Number service sells instant income and employment verification to state agencies determining SNAP, Medicaid and TANF eligibility
researched.notes: A consumer credit bureau whose core business is horizontal — credit and employment data sold to lenders, employers and everyone else. The Work Number reaching state SNAP/Medicaid eligibility offices is a government vertical on a horizontal data asset, the same shape as Dun & Bradstreet. Queues for a person rather than a public card.

researched.name: EXL Health
researched.description: Healthcare data, analytics and operations services — payment integrity, clinical services and risk-adjustment coding — for health plans, provider organizations and life sciences companies.
researched.notes: Rules 2 and 5. Data, analytics and operations services — payment integrity, clinical services, risk-adjustment coding — delivered as outsourced operations, and the buyers are health plans and provider organizations, not public agencies. Services business, healthcare payer market.

researched.name: EY
researched.description: Audit, tax and consulting firm whose government and public sector practice advises agencies on program transformation and operations
researched.notes: Rule 2, same class as Deloitte and KPMG. Audit, tax and consulting firm; the government and public sector practice advises agencies on program transformation and operations. Sells people and hours, no named licensed product.

researched.name: Oracle Health
researched.description: Oracle's cloud healthcare line - EHR, revenue cycle and health data platforms - sold to providers, payers and public health organizations.
researched.notes: Rule 5 plus the horizontal shape. Oracle Health (Cerner) is a real product company, but its EHR, revenue-cycle and health-data platforms are sold overwhelmingly to hospitals, health systems and payers, with public health agencies as one buyer among many — healthcare IT, not government technology. That is the Databricks/Google shape: too horizontal to earn a public card, too much of a product company to bury as a supplier. Queue it for a person.

researched.name: Peraton
researched.description: Mission technology and IT services — cyber, cloud, digital, engineering — for U.S. defense, intelligence, homeland security and federal health agencies.
researched.notes: Rule 2, and named in it by name. Peraton sells mission IT services, engineering and staff hours to federal defense, intelligence, homeland security and health agencies. No licensed product, and the buyer is federal rather than SLED besides.

researched.name: Performant, a Machinify company
researched.description: Technology-enabled healthcare payment integrity - claims audit, eligibility and coordination of benefits, data mining and recovery analytics - for health plans, managed Medicaid plans and government agencies including the CMS RAC program
researched.notes: Rule 2 — a technology-enabled services business, not a product company. Its own site describes contract audit, eligibility, recovery and data-mining engagements (Audit Advantage, TPL Advantage, Recovery Advantage) rather than software licensed to an agency, and the buyers are commercial and Blues health plans, CMS RAC work, and managed Medicaid plans — payer-side payment integrity, not a system a state agency runs its programme on.

researched.name: Progress Software
researched.description: Application development, data platform (MarkLogic, Semaphore) and infrastructure management software for enterprises, sold to government through a Federal Solutions unit.
researched.notes: Horizontal enterprise software — app dev tooling, MarkLogic/Semaphore data platform, infrastructure management — sold to every industry, with a federal arm as one channel. Government is a customer segment, not the product's purpose. Queue for a person.

researched.name: Public Consulting Group
researched.description: Public sector management consulting and operations improvement for state health, education and human services agencies.
researched.notes: Rule 2, named in it explicitly. PCG sells management consulting and operations-improvement hours to state health, education and human services agencies. Deep public-sector revenue does not make it a product company.

researched.name: Public Knowledge
researched.description: Management and IT consulting - systems, programs, people and Medicaid IV&V - for government health, human services, child support and child welfare agencies.
researched.notes: Rule 2. Management and IT consulting for HHS, child support and child welfare agencies, including Medicaid IV&V — IV&V is by definition an independent services engagement, not a licensed product. People and hours.

researched.name: Pulselight
researched.description: AI analytics and case management for fraud, waste and abuse detection and electronic visit verification in Medicaid and other health and human services programs.
researched.notes: Named product: Aura, Torch and Trace. Survives the challenge. I pushed on Rule 2 and Rule 5 and it clears both. Rule 2 (consultancy): the reviewer's named products were not in any local intake record — /Users/wyethwest/govtech-dock/data/proposed_hhs_cards.json and proposed_hhs_cards_4.json contain no 'Aura', 'Torch' or 'Trace' — so I treated the claim as unsupported and fetched pulselight.com directly. The live site confirms all three as named cloud products of a SaaS company, explicitly not a consulting firm: Aura (HHS analytics and incident management), Torch (fraud, waste and abuse) and Trace (EVV analytics against 'EVV, Medica

researched.name: PwC
researched.description: Audit, assurance, tax and consulting firm whose Health Industries practice advises healthcare, pharmaceutical, life sciences and medical device organizations
researched.notes: Rule 2, named in it. Audit, tax and advisory hours; the Health Industries practice advises healthcare, pharma and device organizations. No product, and the described buyer is not even a government agency.

researched.name: Qlarant
researched.description: Fraud, waste and abuse investigation, quality improvement and predictive risk analytics (the RIViR suite) for government health, human services, drug pricing and insurance programs.
researched.notes: Rules 2 and 3 together. Qlarant, Inc. is a not-for-profit parent (formerly Delmarva Foundation) whose business is program-integrity investigation and quality-improvement engagements for CMS, VA and state agencies through Qlarant Integrity Solutions and Qlarant Quality Solutions. The RIViR suite is real and named, but it is marketed as the analytics platform underpinning those service contracts rather than software an agency licenses and runs itself — not enough to earn a public card. Reopenable if someone confirms standalone RIViR licensing to states.

researched.name: Rubrik
researched.description: Backup, data security and cyber-recovery platform for enterprise and government data estates.
researched.notes: Horizontal infrastructure — backup, data security and cyber-recovery for any enterprise data estate, government included. Exactly the Splunk shape. Queue for a person.

researched.name: SAS
researched.description: Analytics, data management and AI software (SAS Viya), including fraud and compliance applications, sold to public sector, health care and commercial customers.
researched.notes: Horizontal analytics and AI software (Viya) sold across commercial, healthcare and public sector alike. The fraud and compliance applications have genuine state-agency traction, but the company is not a govtech product company — it is a general analytics vendor with a public sector vertical. Queue for a person.

researched.name: School of Lunch
researched.description: Multi-day culinary training academy, school-food consulting and change toolkits helping school lunch programs and families move to scratch-cooked, nutrient-dense meals
researched.notes: A services and training business, not a product company. It sells a multi-day culinary training academy, school-food consulting and change toolkits — hours, curriculum and coaching delivered to district nutrition programs. K-12 buyer, but nothing licensed or operated as software.

researched.name: SecureCare
researched.notes: Rule 6 — no site on file, no description, and the name is shared by several unrelated companies (hospice document-management software, a dental benefits carrier, home-care services). I cannot tell what they sell and will not invent it. Needs a human to identify the entity before it can be ruled.

researched.name: ServiceNow
researched.description: Enterprise workflow and AI platform, including Public Sector Digital Services and IT asset and field service management for government agencies.
researched.notes: Horizontal enterprise workflow and AI platform whose core market is the Fortune 500; Public Sector Digital Services is one vertical packaging of the same platform. Government among everyone else — the textbook scope_review shape. Queue for a person.

researched.name: Shift Technology
researched.description: AI decisioning agents for insurance claims - fraud and risk, coverage and liability, subrogation - plus healthcare payment integrity, sold to insurers and health plans.
researched.notes: A product company, but the buyer is wrong: AI decisioning for claims fraud, coverage, liability and subrogation is sold to insurance carriers and health payers, not to state, local or education agencies. Not govtech, and not horizontal-with-government-among-the-buyers either, so it goes to suppliers rather than the review queue.

researched.name: SmartLight Analytics
researched.description: Continuous claims monitoring and clinical review that finds waste, billing errors and overpayments in medical, pharmacy and dental claims for self-funded plan sponsors.
researched.notes: Rule 4, the employer-benefits cut, almost verbatim. It monitors medical, pharmacy and dental claims for self-funded plan sponsors — when a city or district buys this, it buys as an employer watching its own health plan spend, not as an agency running a public programme.

researched.name: InterSystems
researched.description: IRIS data platform and HealthShare health information exchange software for healthcare providers, payers and government agencies.
researched.notes: Horizontal data-platform vendor. IRIS is a general-purpose database and interoperability platform sold across healthcare, financial services and industry; HealthShare is sold to providers, payers and some state HIEs/public health agencies alike. Sells to government among everyone else — the Databricks/Splunk shape. Queue for a person rather than force a call.

researched.name: IronBridge
researched.description: Healthcare data integration (Pub Hub) connecting EHR vendors, pharmacies, laboratories and hospitals to public health systems for vaccine management and electronic reporting.
researched.notes: Rule 5, buyer test. Pub Hub is a real named product — a public health clearinghouse connected to every state immunization registry — but the paying customers are EHR vendors, pharmacies, laboratories, hospitals and long-term care (Epic, PracticeFusion, Azalea Health, PathGroup are cited clients). Providers buy it to meet their own reporting obligations; the public health agency is the destination of the data, not the customer. Health IT sold to private healthcare, not govtech. Worth reopening if they ever sell the registry side to states directly.

researched.name: J. Michael Consulting
researched.description: Public health informatics consulting — laboratory informatics, HL7/FHIR data exchange, epidemiology, data science and project management — for public health agencies and their laboratories.
researched.notes: Rule 2, and the exception does not apply. Sells public health informatics consulting — laboratory informatics, HL7/FHIR data exchange, epidemiology, data science, project management and training. The only named software on their site is Rhapsody, a third-party integration engine they teach a course about rather than license. Revenue is consulting hours.

researched.name: Jama Software
researched.description: Jama Connect requirements management, traceability and risk software for engineering teams in regulated industries, including government and public service programs
researched.notes: Horizontal product. Jama Connect is requirements management and traceability for engineering teams in regulated industries — aerospace, medical devices, automotive, semiconductors — with government and public sector as one vertical among many. A real product company, but not one whose product is sold to SLED agencies as such. Queue for a person.

researched.name: KPMG
researched.description: Audit, tax and advisory firm with a Government and Public Sector practice advising federal, state and local agencies.
researched.notes: Rule 2, named explicitly in the rule. Audit, tax and advisory firm selling people and hours; the Government and Public Sector practice advises agencies but does not license a product to them.

researched.name: Kunz, Leigh & Associates (KL&A)
researched.description: Custom software for state agencies: WIC management information systems, Medicaid third-party-liability modules, FOIA request management and government mass notification.
researched.notes: Rule 2, and the closest call in this batch. They do build systems state agencies run programmes on — a WIC MIS with a Vendor Management module, Medicaid third-party-liability modules, FOIA request management, and MiCaRS serving 16 State of Michigan agencies. But their own homepage brands them a Custom Software Development Company selling custom software development, mobile app development and professional consulting, and I could not confirm a distinct product brand licensed across multiple states (their WIC page failed TLS verification). A bespoke development shop, not a product company. Torn

researched.name: Leidos
researched.description: Systems integration and IT services across defense, intelligence, homeland, energy infrastructure and health, sold primarily to US federal government customers.
researched.notes: Rule 2, same kind as GDIT and Peraton which the rule names. Systems integration and IT services across defense, intelligence, homeland, energy and health, sold primarily to US federal agencies. Sells people and hours, and the buyer is mostly federal rather than SLED.

researched.name: MedImpact
researched.description: Independent pharmacy benefit manager for commercial health plans, government health programs and self-insured employer groups.
researched.notes: Rule 4, the employer-benefits cut. An independent pharmacy benefit manager serving commercial health plans, self-insured employers and government health programs. A PBM administers drug benefits for a plan; it is not a system a government agency runs its programmes on. PBMs are supplier by rule.

researched.name: MedReview
researched.description: Physician-led payment integrity - DRG coding and clinical validation review, hospital bill audits, readmission review - plus HEDIS/QARR and Medicaid managed care quality assessments for health plans and government agencies
researched.notes: Services business. Physician-led payment integrity — DRG coding and clinical validation review, hospital bill audits, readmission review — plus HEDIS/QARR reporting. Clinicians reviewing claims on behalf of payers is expert-hours work, not a licensed system, even where a state Medicaid programme is the client.

researched.name: Morgan & Morgan
researched.notes: Law firm. No site or description on file, but the name is the national personal-injury plaintiffs' firm — nothing about it is a technology product, and law firms are supplier by rule. This is exactly the company that must not land on a public job board for government technology sales roles.

researched.name: Myers & Stauffer
researched.description: Medicaid audit and payment-integrity services - provider cost audits, claims and eligibility reviews, estate recovery, managed care audits - for state health and human services agencies.
researched.notes: Rule 2 and the accounting/audit-firm clause. A CPA firm selling Medicaid audit and payment-integrity services — provider cost audits, claims and eligibility reviews, estate recovery, managed care audits — to state agencies. Sells hours and audit opinions, not software.

researched.name: NCCI
researched.description: Unannounced pre- and post-enrollment provider site visits and field inspections for state Medicaid agencies and CMS contractors, alongside collateral and occupancy inspections for lenders and insurers.
researched.notes: Services business. Sells unannounced pre- and post-enrollment provider site visits and field inspections to state Medicaid agencies and CMS contractors — fieldwork performed by people, plus collateral services. A real and relevant government contractor, but the deliverable is labor, not a product agencies license. (Note: this is ncciservices.com, not the workers-comp rating bureau of the same initials.)

researched.name: North Highland
researched.description: Management and technology consulting - data and systems modernization, transformation management and workforce optimization - for state health and human services agencies and other public sector clients
researched.notes: Rule 2. Management and technology consulting — data and systems modernization, transformation management, workforce optimization — for state health and human services and other agencies. Sells consultants and hours; no named licensed product.

researched.name: NTT DATA
researched.description: IT modernization, cloud, cybersecurity, application and consulting services for federal, state and local government and education agencies.
researched.notes: Rule 2. The cited page is their government consulting and advisory practice, and the offering is entirely services: IT modernization, cloud, cybersecurity, application development and consulting for federal, state, local and education. A systems integrator selling people and hours, the GDIT/Accenture shape.

researched.name: Optimoz
researched.description: Optimoz AI, an enterprise platform for building, running and governing autonomous AI agents, sold to federal government, healthcare, higher education and enterprise customers.
researched.notes: Horizontal product, and thin evidence of a SLED buyer. Optimoz AI is positioned as an Enterprise Agentic AI Operating System for building, running and governing autonomous agents, with the pitch aimed at regulated enterprise deployment (HIPAA, SOC 2, data sovereignty, on-prem) across federal government, healthcare, higher education and commercial. Federal-leaning and sells to everyone; also historically a DevSecOps services firm, so what they now sell is genuinely ambiguous. Queue for a person.

researched.name: Optum
